items.title: Ancient “living fossils” may reveal how complex life began

Scientists think similar partnerships billions of years ago may have helped produce the first complex cells.

items.title: NASA scientists discover a giant 10-sided pattern on Saturn

items.title: The universe has plenty of hydrogen. So why is star formation collapsing?
items.summary_raw: Star formation across the universe has fallen dramatically over the past 4.5 billion years, but astronomers have uncovered a surprising twist: the supply of neutral hydrogen, a key ingredient for making stars, has barely declined. Using China’s FAST radio telescope and data from roughly 2.5 million galaxies observed by DESI, researchers found that star formation was about 2.5 times higher 4.5 billion years ago, while neutral hydrogen levels were only about 1.4 times higher.

items.title: Each extra hour of prolonged sitting linked to 9% higher cancer death risk

Breaking up sitting with movement showed the opposite pattern, while replacing an hour of prolonged sitting with light activity was linked to a 12% lower risk.
